title: "Java is not defined" reported by Jupyter notebook
question:
I have jdk v17 and v23 both installed and both are in configured in Windows 11 Environment System variable path. Error: (1) when I type "Java -version" at windows cmd I see only v23 installed (2) when I type "Java -version" in my jupyter notebook, I see the message "NameError: name 'java' is not defined. I have hadoop, python also installedenter image description here.

Hope to keep both JDK and use one for some application and other for a different application.
answer:
Jupyter notebooks execute source code. java -version is something you'd run on the command line. So Jupyter is trying to compile or interp your java code. If you were to enter this into a java source file and run it through the compiler it thinks java is a variable and - is the subtraction operator. So Java would think you wrote java - version as in variable named java minus variable named version. Hence name java is not defined because all variables in Java would need to be defined with a type declaration and a name (ie Integer x).

If you want to know the version of Java in Jupyter do the following:

System.out.println( System.getProperty("java.version") )

Note: when you type java -version on the command line you are going to see the version of java that windows is using when you type the command java. You may have other versions of Java installed on your machine, but your OS is only going to use 1 of them when executing the java command. If you want to switch to another version you need to change your environment variables to point JAVA_HOME environment variable to a different path. In fact if you execute the following you can see where the current version of Java is installed.

> echo %JAVA_HOME%

By changing that environment variable you can point it to JDK17 if you prefer, but you'll have to restart your command line windows and programs that executing (ie Jupyter)

If you added the path to the JVM's home directory to the PATH directly you can see it doing:

> echo %PATH%

Changing %JAVA_HOME% is the preferred method. But, if that doesn't work check your %PATH% variable for possible hard coding.
